provenance.canonical_layout: SEC XBRL company-concept payloads captured verbatim from data.sec.gov for the balance-sheet concepts (cash and cash equivalents, current marketable securities, commercial paper, long-term debt non-current and long-term debt current), plus the canonical daily price series and filing acceptance index reused by path from data/historical_pe/AAPL and the cover-page shares outstanding series reused by path from data/historical_pfcf/AAPL. The trailing revenue and EBITDA denominators are the data/historical_income/AAPL dataset own windows, executed from its config, never recomputed here.

concept_fetch.transport: HTTPS GET data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK0000320193/us-gaap/{tag}.json with a declared contactable User-Agent, honouring the SEC fair-access policy
concept_fetch.response_units: verbatim as returned: USD for all five balance-sheet concepts

cash_concept.json.definition: Cash and cash equivalents at carrying value, the liquid-funds component of the filed EV bridge.

marketable_securities_current_concept.js.definition: Current marketable securities, the second liquid-funds component of the filed EV bridge. First carried from FY2018 filings, so earlier evaluation dates have an incomplete bridge and no EV.

commercial_paper_concept.json.definition: Commercial paper, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge alongside the two long-term debt concepts.

long_term_debt_noncurrent_concept.json.definition: Non-current long-term debt, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge.

long_term_debt_current_concept.json.definition: Current long-term debt, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge. First carried from FY2014 filings.

daily_prices.json (reused by path).source: The canonical production historical P/E price series, read by path. The trading calendar decides when a filing's fact becomes knowable under the 16:00 ET cutoff rule, so one calendar serves every reconstruction.

filing_acceptance_evidence.json (reused.source: The canonical SGML-header acceptance index, read by path. A fact whose filing is not in the index has no knowability evidence in this dataset and is skipped.

shares_outstanding_concept.json (reused.source: The canonical cover-page shares outstanding series from the historical P/FCF dataset, read by path so one share series serves every market-cap reconstruction. Counts are never split-adjusted and pair with the as-traded close.

provenance.point_in_time_rule: usable_date is derived from acceptance_datetime_header_et using the 16:00 ET cutoff rule at load time, identical to the historical P/E, P/FCF and income pipelines. The value in force at an evaluation date is the latest knowable version of each component; no fact is used before its filing usable date.

multiple_rules.ps: P/S = (as-traded close on the evaluation date x latest knowable cover-page shares outstanding) / TTM revenue, where the TTM revenue window is the income dataset own four-consecutive-fiscal-quarter window. A non-positive denominator produces no multiple.
multiple_rules.ev_ebitda: EV/EBITDA = (market capitalization + total debt [long-term debt non-current + long-term debt current + commercial paper] - liquid funds [cash + current marketable securities]) / TTM EBITDA. Every bridge component must be knowable at the evaluation date; a date with any component missing has no EV and the bridge is never completed by omission, substitution or zero-fill. The bridge remains a partial statement of enterprise value (it omits leases, non-current investments and off-balance sheet claims) and every observation says so.

provenance.reference_gate: The same >= 20 qualifying observations rule as every other production distribution. A thinner sample stays descriptive and is never a scenario exit multiple.
known_limitations: The bridge components start at different dates (long-term debt FY2014, current marketable securities FY2018), so early evaluation dates have an incomplete bridge and no EV/EBITDA while P/S may still compute.
The reconstructed enterprise value omits operating leases under ASC 842, non-current investments and off-balance sheet commitments; it is labelled partial on every observation.
The evaluation dates are the income dataset filing usable dates, not a continuous daily trading history.
